title: [23/01/2024] Australian road tunnels
prompt: The diagrams below give information about two road tunnels in two Australian cities. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagrams illustrate the key features and specifications of two road tunnels constructed in different Australian cities, showing their design, construction details, and operational characteristics.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while both tunnels share the same length, Tunnel B was significantly more expensive to construct and required more complex engineering due to the challenging geological conditions. Additionally, Tunnel A was built earlier and operates underwater through sand, whereas Tunnel B was constructed later through stone and clay at a greater depth.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding Tunnel A, this infrastructure project was constructed between 1986 and 1998 at a cost of $555 million. The tunnel operates at a depth of 1.5 meters below the surface, passing through sand material. Its design features two separate tubes to accommodate bi-directional traffic flow, with each tube handling vehicles traveling in opposite directions.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, Tunnel B represents a more recent and complex engineering undertaking, built between 2002 and 2006 with a substantially higher budget of $1.1 billion. This tunnel extends to a depth of 2.5 meters, which is one meter deeper than Tunnel A, and was excavated through more challenging geological conditions consisting of stone and clay. The design incorporates three separate tubes, suggesting enhanced capacity or additional safety features compared to the two-tube configuration of Tunnel A.
